drivingQuestion: Why is the fifteenth of Av a day of joy?
outcomeNote: the unit ends mid-question; the 'but 15 Av, why?' half lies in the next unit

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב וּכְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים. בִּשְׁלָמָא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים — מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ סְלִיחָה וּמְחִילָה, יוֹם שֶׁנִּיתְּנוּ בּוֹ לוּחוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנוֹת.
segments.en: § The mishna taught that «Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no days as happy for the Jewish people as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur.» The Gemara asks: «Granted, Yom Kippur» is a day of joy «because it has» the elements of «pardon and forgiveness,» and moreover, it is the «day on which the last» pair of «tablets were given.»
